business_scope.primary_industry_name: Specialty Fresh Bakery Master Franchise and Central Kitchen Ops

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Bijural hybrid: federal Common Law public order superimposed on Quebec Civil Law private law tradition; codified statutes (Quebec Civil Code, CQLR) govern corporate existence and commercial obligations.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (Canada-China FIPA), signed 9 September 2012, in force 1 October 2014

Agreement between the Government of Canada and the Government of the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income, signed 12 May 1986, amended by Protocol of 21 October 2009 (Canada-China DTA, in force 2010)
WTO General Agreement on Trade in Services and Trade-Related Investment Measures (both states WTO members; no sector-specific preferential treatment for bakery franchise master licensing)
No CPTPP or bilateral free-trade agreement applies to a China-headquartered franchisor (Canada is a CPTPP member; China is not)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: 1) Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184 (FINTRAC reporting, CDD, beneficial ownership verification for regulated entities); 2) Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.3-462.5 (money-laundering predicates), s. 354, s. 355.1; 3) Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1, arts. 39.1-39.11 (obligatory register of individuals having significant control and officer certification duty); 4) Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 10.2.2, 34.1 (annual declaration to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec disclosing significant-control persons and Quebec head-office address); 5) Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 21.1 (federal ISC register, applicable only if the federal vehicle is selected instead of provincial incorporation); 6) FINTRAC Guidance on Politically Exposed Persons (PEP), Beneficial Ownership, and Know Your Client requirements.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / continued existence of the Chinese franchisor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / market supervision administrative department
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Chinese Foreign Affairs Office chain of authentication, plus notarization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies of all directors, shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC notary public (公证处) in the administrative region of the owner's domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Chinese Foreign Affairs Office chain of authentication)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Audited financial statements of the Chinese master franchisor (last two fiscal years), notarially certified
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC certified public accounting firm with notarization by local 公证处
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Chinese Foreign Affairs Office chain of authentication)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (委任书) appointing the Quebec incorporation agent / local representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Chinese Foreign Affairs Office chain of authentication); may be supplemented by Quebec notarial certification if executed in Quebec

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, officers and UBOs against: (i) OFAC SDN and Consolidated Non-SDN Lists (US), (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (under Special Economic Measures Act, Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, Sergei Magnitsky Law, and United Nations Act), (iv) UK and EU consolidated lists for cross-border banking tolerance; PEP designation and family/close-associate analysis under FINTRAC Guidance (PEPs of domestic and foreign origin); sanctions approval determination via Global Affairs Canada enforcement framework; domestic CDD standard requiring police criminal record check for non-resident directors. For a Low_Risk_Standard bakery franchise, standard CDD applies with a FINTRAC compliance program (designated AML officer, risk assessment, written procedures, training, STR/EFTR reporting).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Registre central des entreprises (RCEQ) - online filing portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca (Services en ligne / Nom d'entreprise - analyse et réservation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), the corporate name of a Quebec company must be in French; a French version of the name must be registered and must predominate in public signage, contracts, invoices and commercial documents. A non-French version (e.g., Chinese or English trade name) may be added, but only as a secondary version and only after a compliant French version is reserved; transliteration of a Chinese brand into Pinyin does not by itself constitute a French name. The French name must contain a distinctive element, a descriptive element (optional) and a legal element ('inc.', 'corp.', 'ltée').
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank — reserved for federally licensed banks (Bank Act); prior Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) authorization required
Assurance / Insurance / Assurances — requires prior authorization from the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF)
Fiducie / Trust — restricted; requires AMF license
Université / Collège / Académie — requires prior approval of the Ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur
Ordre / Chambre professionnelle — suggests a professional order; restricted
Royal / Royale / Reine / Crown — suggests state affiliation; requires prior government approval
Coopérative / Société coopérative — prohibited unless the entity is actually formed and registered as a cooperative
Fondation — restricted; implies charitable status requiring registration under the Civil Code or Income Tax Act
Gendarmerie / Police / Milice — prohibited as misleading public-order connotation
Québec (as first word implying governmental entity), Canada, Ministère, Commission — authorized only with ministerial consent
Any name that is deceptive, contrary to public order, or comprises expressions prohibited by QBCA art. 27(3) — absolute general prohibition
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon REQ name refusal, the applicant may: (1) amend the proposed name (refiling the name analysis request with a new distinctive element and re-payment of the analysis fee) and re-submit the incorporation file; (2) within 30 days of the refusal decision, file a written rectification/reconsideration request with the REQ identifying the legal error or new facts (decision rendered on the record); (3) appeal the reconsideration refusal to the Court of Québec (civil litigation route) within 30 days of notification, with a copy served on the Registraire; (4) alternatively, reserve the refused name in translated form or abandon provincial incorporation in favor of a federal CBCA incorporation with a Quebec head office if the NUANS search yields a compliant name — the federal path does not override the Charter of the French Language signage rules.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. Quebec law (QBCA, art. 22) requires the head office to be situated at a geographic address in Quebec, which must be a legitimate physical location where process can be served; the REQ will reject a P.O. box only, but a virtual office with dedicated reception staff, physical address, document scanning and process-agent availability is generally acceptable for a master-franchise holding entity. However, a central kitchen operator must maintain an actual production establishment with a municipal occupancy permit and MAPAQ hygiene registration; the virtual office can serve only administrative/registered-agent purposes and does not satisfy food-business establishment requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: (i) REQ/registered-office address verification — 10% probability of unannounced check in year one; (ii) municipal zoning and building inspection for the central kitchen — 95% probability before first production; (iii) Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation (MAPAQ) food establishment inspection — certain (100%) upon license issuance; (iv) Revenu Québec GST/QST registration verification visit — 20-30% probability in the first 12 months.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1, sections 3, 16, 18, 22, 30-32, 43-46 and 78-79; extra-provincial recognition under section 19 of the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c C-44, if federal articles are elected.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ); Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) for federal CBCA registration if the provincial-registered federal route is chosen.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts constitutifs) filed electronically through the Registraire’s OneStop Business Registration portal and registered under the Quebec Business Corporations Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement for a QBCA corporation; directors determine share consideration. No escrow or paid-in capital holdback is required for a standard bakery corporate vehicle, but issued shares must be fully credited before share certificates are delivered.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: (1) the articles of incorporation filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec are adopted in final form; (2) the share subscriptions recorded in the subscription ledger are accepted and the directors are authorized to issue the designated common shares upon receipt of valid consideration; (3) the registered office is established at the address stated in the articles, where the corporate minute book, registers and corporate seal will be maintained; (4) the persons named in the officer appointment schedule are appointed Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, each to hold office at the pleasure of the board; and (5) the officers may open financial institution accounts and execute regulatory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) / Corporations Canada (ISED) for federal name approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a NUANS name search report for the proposed French or bilingual corporate name. Submit a name reservation request through the REQ OneStop portal or, if selecting a federal CBCA corporation, through Corporations Canada online. Ensure the name includes the required legal element 'Inc.' or 'Corp.' and does not contain reserved or prohibited words for a bakery franchise. Keep the reservation receipt with the dossier. Notarization is not required for name reservation; a notarized power of attorney is required if filing is made by a third-party agent.
required_dossiers: Name search and reservation fee receipt
Notarized power of attorney, if acting through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ or Corporations Canada refuses the name, the applicant may file an amended name reservation with a new proposed name. The refusal notice will identify the conflicting name; no fee refund applies, but the amended filing may be processed on a priority basis.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Filing Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — OneStop Business Registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit the articles of incorporation (statuts constitutifs) in the REQ electronic filing system. Include share classes and rights, director count, and registered office address. The incorporator must sign the articles; digital signature is accepted for online filing. Pay the prescribed filing fee and obtain the certificate of incorporation and enterprise number (NEQ). If paper filing is used for a non-resident incorporator, the signature must be notarized or accompanied by a consular certification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ returns the filing for correction, the incorporator must cure deficiencies within 30 days. Amendments to the articles must be refiled electronically; the original filing fee is retained and no additional fee is charged for the first correction if submitted timely.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Adoption of Initial Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation / Corporate Secretariat
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and adopt the pro-forma first board resolution. Set up the statutory corporate minute book, share subscription ledger, directors’ register, officers’ register and corporate seal. Confirm the registered office in Quebec and issue share certificates after the consideration is recorded. Ensure the minutes are signed by all directors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If minutes contain procedural defects, the board may adopt a correcting resolution and replace the defective pages of the minutes book. The registered office address may be changed online through REQ before any third-party reliance occurs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Registration with REQ and Tax Account Activation with Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) / Revenu Québec (OneStop synchronization)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Through the OneStop portal, ensure the newly incorporated company is registered as a Quebec enterprise and obtain the NEQ. Simultaneously activate Revenu Québec accounts for QST, GST/HST, source deductions and employer contributions. The portal transmits data to Revenu Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency for a federal corporation. Provide the registered office address and director information. No notarization is required for tax registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If activation is delayed, file a request for a retroactive effective date with Revenu Québec. Where penalties arise, the corporation may invoke due-diligence and good-faith remedial filing under Revenu Québec’s administrative relief policy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Return, Annual Declaration and Municipal Operating Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec / Revenu Québec / Local City Borough Permit Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 60 days after incorporation, file the initial return under the QBCA with REQ and, if applicable, the federal initial return with Corporations Canada. Thereafter, maintain the annual declaration and other statutory registers. Apply to the municipal borough for a commercial occupancy permit for the pastry shop and central kitchen before fit-out begins; provide the lease, floor plan and food establishment application.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A late initial return can trigger dissolution proceedings by REQ. File the overdue declaration with a formal explanation and, if necessary, submit a regularization application; in severe cases, apply for reinstatement before the registrar proceeds with administrative dissolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ) — Food Inspection and Food Establishment Licensing Branch
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Establishment Permit (Certificat d'établissement alimentaire) under the Food Products Act, RLRQ c P-29

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA for a midsize bakery central kitchen under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c Q-2; however, registration or authorization may be required if process wastewater discharge exceeds prescribed municipal or provincial volumetric thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: BOD5 ≤ 500 mg/L, total suspended solids ≤ 600 mg/L and oil/grease ≤ 100 mg/L, unless the host municipality imposes stricter limits; any discharge exceeding municipal capacity requires MELCCFP section 22 authorization. Air emissions: oven combustion and ventilation must comply with the Clean Air Regulation, CQLR c Q-2, r 4.1, including smoke opacity, particulate and odour limits. Organic waste: storage and disposal must comply with the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of organic materials, CQLR c Q-2, r 19.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a fire safety certificate from the local fire prevention service confirming compliance with the Fire Safety Act and Building Act; provide a structural load inspection certificate issued by a Quebec-engineer for oven lines and chilled storage areas; register with the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST), obtain a workplace health and safety clearance notice, and post the safety policy as required under the Act respecting occupational health and safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC), with Business Registration Online (BRO) and the My Business Account portal at canada.ca. Provincial: Revenu Quebec, with the Mon dossier d'entreprise portal at revenuquebec.ca; under the single-administration agreement, Revenu Quebec administers both QST and GST/HST for Quebec-establishment registrants, and the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) is the provincial registration anchor.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Business Corporations Act (Quebec) via Corporations Canada or the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec; obtain Articles of Incorporation and, for Quebec, the NEQ. Step 2: Obtain the federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1, and enrol the necessary program accounts, including RT (GST/HST), RP (payroll), and RC (corporate income tax). Step 3: Register for GST/HST as soon as taxable supplies in Canada exceed CAD 30,000 in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters or when a first taxable supply is made after ceasing to qualify as a small supplier; registration is also mandatory, without the small-supplier threshold, for non-resident digital/e-commerce suppliers using fulfillment warehouses or making specified digital supplies. Step 4: Register for QST with Revenu Quebec within 30 days of losing small-supplier status, using the combined federal-provincial registration form; obtain the TQ program account formatted as NEQ + TQ + number. Step 5: Enrol for CRA payroll and/or provincial employer accounts (Quebec Parental Insurance Plan, CNESST, workforce skills development) where headcount applies. Step 6: Open a CAD settlement account and activate CRA My Business Account and Revenu Quebec Clavier mobile credential for electronic filings and notices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Business Corporation is a distinct taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act and the Quebec Taxation Act; it has no pass-through eligibility, and shareholders are taxed only on dividends or capital gains. Territorial_Scope: a Canadian-resident corporation is taxable on worldwide income; a non-resident corporation is taxable on Canadian-source employment income, business income carried on in Canada, and taxable Canadian property gains. Tax_Exempt_Zone: none; no Canadian province offers an income tax exemption zone, although customs duty relief is available through bonded warehouses and customs-controlled areas. The corporation is eligible for the Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction only if owned by Canadian residents, with the federal 9% and Quebec 3.2% reduced rates on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, subject to associated-corporation and taxable-capital limits; where foreign ownership applies, the general combined rate of 26.5% (federal 15% plus Quebec 11.5%) applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Canada; an incorporated entity cannot elect partnership or flow-through treatment. Material elections and statutory mechanisms include: (1) allocation agreement among associated corporations under subsection 125(6) of the Income Tax Act to divide the CAD 500,000 small business limit; (2) the refundable dividend tax on hand election under subsection 129(7) for dividend refund planning; (3) the section 216 election for a non-resident owning Canadian rental real estate to be taxed on net rental income rather than Part XIII gross withholding; (4) voluntary GST/HST and QST registration under section 240 of the Excise Tax Act even before the small-supplier threshold is crossed, allowing input tax credit recovery; and (5) OECD hybrid mismatch measures, which are mandatory anti-avoidance rules in the Income Tax Act (effective primarily for payments made after June 30, 2023, and mirrored under the Quebec Taxation Act) that deny deductions or require inclusion where hybrid instruments or entities produce deduction/non-inclusion outcomes or duplicate deductions. No election can oust these hybrid-mismatch provisions.

corporate_income_tax_context.residency_basis: Resident corporation taxed on worldwide income; foreign-derived active business income is generally taxable in Canada, with foreign tax credits available, and controlled foreign affiliate FAPI rules apply to passive income of foreign affiliates.
corporate_income_tax_context.non_resident_withholding_notes: Where a foreign parent or foreign licensor receives dividends from the Canadian corporation, Part XIII withholding applies at 25% gross, treaty-reduced to 5% for a China-resident parent holding at least 10% of voting shares under Article 10 of the Canada-China Income Tax Convention; royalties and interest are generally treaty-reduced to 10%; all transfer-pricing arrangements must satisfy arm's length standards under sections 247 of the Income Tax Act and 42.6 of the Quebec Taxation Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual federal-provincial value-added tax: federal GST/HST at 5% and Quebec QST at 9.5% computed on the GST-inclusive selling price, producing a combined effective headline rate of 14.975%. Canada does not operate a US-style sales and use tax; GST/HST and QST are multi-stage VAT systems with full input tax credit mechanisms.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (the small-supplier threshold under section 148 of the Excise Tax Act and the equivalent QST provision; same CAD 30,000 threshold applies to QST). A person who ceases to be a small supplier at any time must register within 30 days, and, once registered, must collect tax on all subsequent taxable supplies. Non-resident suppliers of specified digital services or goods delivered through a distribution platform/fulfillment warehouse in Canada have mandated registration independent of the CAD 30,000 threshold, effective as of July 1, 2021, for GST/HST and QST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or certification-of-invoice regime. CRA and Revenu Quebec accept paper, EDI, PDF, and structured XML invoices; the Pan-Canadian Peppol interoperability framework is voluntary in business-to-government and business-to-business procurement, not a tax clearance requirement. A compliant tax invoice must contain the supplier's BN (and QST registration number), the purchaser's name, the date, a description of the supply, the GST/HST and QST amounts or rates, and the total consideration; these data elements are the gateway to the purchaser's input tax credit claim under subsection 169(4) of the Excise Tax Act and section 25 of the Quebec Sales Tax Act. No API-based tax authority clearance or digital fiscal seal is required before a sale.

supply_characterization_for_bakery_franc.take_away_bakery_goods: Zero-rated as basic groceries under Schedule VI, Part II of the Excise Tax Act and the corresponding QST schedule, including fresh bread, pastries, buns, bagels, muffins, cakes, and Chinese-style baked goods, provided the supply is not made as a restaurant meal, not served for immediate consumption on the vendor's premises, and not packaged as a taxable snack food.
supply_characterization_for_bakery_franc.in_store_cafe_seating: Taxable at the standard rate where food or beverages are supplied for consumption on the premises of the bakery, café area, or any chair-and-table service zone operated by the corporation or a franchisee.
supply_characterization_for_bakery_franc.central_kitchen_supplies_to_franchisees: Sales by the central kitchen of unbaked, frozen, or take-away bakery products to franchisees for downstream take-away resale are generally zero-rated; the franchisee's sit-down café sales are taxable at the standard rate and attract QST and GST on the full retail selling price.
supply_characterization_for_bakery_franc.royalties_and_management_fees: Master franchise royalties, franchise fees, and management services supplied to Canadian resident franchisees are standard-rated supplies subject to GST/QST at the combined 14.975% effective rate; the same supplies made to non-resident franchisees for use entirely outside Canada may be zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, section 7 of the Excise Tax Act as services supplied to a non-resident, subject to the statutory carve-outs for services in relation to Canadian real property and goods.
supply_characterization_for_bakery_franc.wage_and_payroll_nexus: The corporation's payroll or fixed place of business in Quebec establishes a permanent establishment for QST/GST purposes and triggers mandatory registration even if the CAD 30,000 threshold were not met.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no general foreign-exchange administration imposing capital-account controls. Financial institutions, money services businesses, and payment service providers may also be subject to the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, FINTRAC requirements, sanctions legislation, and applicable Bank of Canada payment-system and retail-payment-supervision rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for ordinary commercial, current-account, and capital-account transactions. Canada generally has no approval requirement, exchange-control quota, mandatory conversion of foreign currency, or restriction on repatriation of paid-in capital, dividends, royalties, management fees, loan principal, or interest. Remittances remain subject to corporate-law authorization, solvency requirements, beneficial-ownership and source-of-funds checks, sanctions screening, transfer-pricing rules, thin-capitalization rules, withholding tax, treaty eligibility, and supporting commercial documentation. A Canadian corporation may maintain foreign-currency accounts and retain export receipts offshore or domestically, subject to bank policies, tax reporting, accounting, and anti-money-laundering controls. Payments to non-residents may generally require Canadian withholding tax, commonly at the 25% statutory rate unless reduced or eliminated under an applicable tax treaty and properly documented.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no mandatory surrender of export proceeds, no statutory conversion ratio, and no general deadline requiring exporters to convert foreign-currency receipts into Canadian dollars. Exporters must comply with customs, sanctions, tax, accounting, and contractual reporting obligations. Goods exports generally require appropriate Canada Border Services Agency reporting, while services, franchise fees, royalties, and other intangible-related receipts must be supported by contracts, invoices, and tax records. Foreign-currency receipts should be reconciled to invoices and bank statements, and foreign-exchange gains or losses should be recorded under applicable Canadian accounting and tax rules. The corporation should separately assess GST/HST treatment, non-resident withholding, transfer pricing, and foreign-asset reporting where relevant.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for supplementary payment functionality and Low as a replacement for a primary Canadian corporate bank. An offshore electronic-money institution may be usable for limited collections, card acquiring, foreign-currency conversion, or vendor payments only if its licensing, territorial permissions, correspondent-bank access, sanctions controls, and Canadian regulatory status are acceptable. The provider must not conduct regulated payment, money-services, remittance, or deposit-taking activity in Canada without the required registration, authorization, or exemption. Relevant regimes may include FINTRAC registration and compliance obligations for money-services activity and the Retail Payment Activities Act for covered payment-service activities. Offshore EMI balances may not provide Canadian deposit-insurance protection and may be restricted by Canadian banks, payment networks, franchise counterparties, or tax auditors. Maintain a Canadian operating account as the primary treasury and settlement account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not universally required by statute to appear physically at a branch. Canadian banks may permit remote onboarding using certified corporate documents, electronic identity verification, video interviews, digital signatures, and a Canadian or international relationship manager. Physical attendance, notarization, an in-person interview, or a Canadian-resident signing officer may nevertheless be required under the bank's risk policy, particularly where ownership is non-resident, the structure uses nominee or holding companies, the business has high cash turnover, the beneficial owner is located in a higher-risk jurisdiction, or the bank cannot independently verify identity and control. Quebec corporations should expect collection of incorporation documents, corporate registers, directors and officers, beneficial-ownership information, business-purpose evidence, and proof of address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership, layered holding companies, nominee shareholders, or inconsistent ownership information across corporate records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified articles and certificates of incorporation, current corporate profile, shareholder register, securities register, organizational chart to the ultimate natural persons, beneficial-ownership declaration, director and officer register, shareholder identity documents, proof of residential address, and signed ownership attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or shareholders, foreign parent funding, or a business model involving cross-border royalty and franchise payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolutions, business plan, franchise and licensing agreements, parent-company organizational chart, audited or management financial statements, source-of-funds memorandum, bank statements, capital contribution agreements, intercompany loan agreements, tax-residency certificates, and documented economic rationale for the Quebec operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained cash-intensive activity, high-volume POS settlements, unusual refunds, chargebacks, third-party deposits, or payment flows inconsistent with a bakery and central-kitchen business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Store and central-kitchen lease agreements, POS and processor contracts, projected sales by location, daily cash-handling procedures, cash-deposit logs, inventory and supplier records, payroll records, sales-tax registrations, franchise revenue schedules, expected transaction profile, and internal fraud and anti-money-laundering controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wires lacking a clear invoice, contract, beneficiary relationship, or commercial purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed invoices, purchase orders, bills of lading where applicable, customs records, franchise and royalty agreements, service agreements, transfer-pricing support, payment-purpose description, beneficiary ownership information, and reconciliation from invoice through bank statement and general ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned persons, sanctioned jurisdictions, high-risk intermediaries, or restricted goods and services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty due-diligence file, sanctions-screening evidence, beneficial-owner verification, end-use and end-user certification, shipping and customs documentation, contractual sanctions clauses, escalation records, and documented legal approval for any permitted transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore fintech accounts, virtual-asset providers, personal accounts, or unrelated third-party wallets for corporate receipts or disbursements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provider licensing and regulatory-status evidence, account ownership confirmation, transaction statements, source-and-destination mapping, board-approved treasury policy, documented business necessity, wallet and counterparty due diligence where applicable, and a commitment to route primary activity through regulated Canadian accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected activity materially exceeding the profile stated during onboarding or rapid movement of recently injected capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling 12-month cash-flow forecast, capital budget, store-opening schedule, financing documents, investor source-of-wealth evidence, board approvals, vendor contracts, payroll forecast, tax filings, and written explanation of temporary transaction spikes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to demonstrate Quebec operating substance, beneficial control, or the commercial need for the account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec business registration, municipal and food-sector permits where applicable, lease or ownership evidence, utility records, employee and payroll records, supplier contracts, website and franchise materials, management biographies, customer and vendor lists, and evidence of central-kitchen or retail operations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route paid-in capital through a Canadian bank account in the exact legal name of the Quebec or federal corporation. Use an international wire, generally SWIFT MT103 or the bank's ISO 20022 equivalent, from an account owned by the shareholder or documented funding entity. The payment narrative should identify the corporation, capital contribution or shareholder loan status, currency, and board-approved transaction reference. Before receipt, provide the bank with the subscription or contribution agreement, board and shareholder resolutions, beneficial-owner information, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, parent-company financial statements, and any intercompany loan or transfer-pricing documentation. Reconcile the wire to the general ledger and issue the appropriate corporate accounting entry. Canada does not use a general statutory FX purpose-code system for ordinary capital inflows; the bank may nevertheless require an internal payment-purpose code, Canadian Payments Association or correspondent-bank data, and tax classification. Do not mix equity, shareholder loans, franchise royalties, and operating receipts in a single unexplained transfer. Retain documentation for Canadian corporate, tax, AML, and audit periods.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use regulated Canadian bank wires for suppliers, equipment, ingredients, logistics providers, franchise licensors, and service providers. SWIFT MT103 or the bank's ISO 20022 customer-credit-transfer equivalent is appropriate for direct payments; identify the beneficiary, invoice number, contract, goods or service description, currency, and charges allocation. For higher-value or documentary transactions, use a commercial letter of credit issued or confirmed by a bank, with documentary collection or open-account settlement only after counterparty risk assessment. Trade-finance files should include purchase orders, invoices, transport documents, customs records, insurance documents, sanctions screening, beneficial-owner checks, and proof of delivery where relevant. Apply Canadian sanctions, export-control, customs, GST/HST, transfer-pricing, and non-resident withholding analysis before payment. Franchise royalties, management fees, interest, and other payments to non-residents should be reviewed for withholding tax, treaty relief, arm's-length pricing, and beneficial-ownership requirements. Use dual authorization, segregated payment preparation and release, beneficiary-change callbacks, transaction limits, and daily bank-to-ledger reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign-exchange contracts for forecast or committed CAD/USD, CAD/CNY, CAD/EUR, or other documented exposures, subject to the bank's credit approval, ISDA or local master agreement, confirmations, collateral terms, and evidence of an underlying commercial exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies that are not freely deliverable or where the bank offers cash-settled hedging, subject to counterparty eligibility, applicable Canadian derivatives rules, reporting, suitability, sanctions, and documentation requirements. NDFs should not be used to evade foreign-exchange controls or disguise speculative transfers.

Foreign-currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for documented funding, liquidity, or long-term currency-mismatch exposures, subject to bank approval, derivatives documentation, valuation, collateral, accounting, and applicable regulatory reporting.

Foreign-exchange spot transactions for ordinary conversion of receipts, supplier payments, payroll, taxes, and repatriation. Maintain an exposure register, hedge-approval policy, counterparty limits, hedge-accounting assessment, and board-approved prohibition or limits on unsupported speculation.

Currency options and option strategies may be available from regulated Canadian banks for documented exposures, but they require enhanced suitability, pricing, liquidity, premium, accounting, and derivatives-risk review. The corporation should obtain legal, tax, and accounting confirmation before execution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) — applicable to a federally incorporated corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation, amalgamation, or continuation; the anniversary date is the relevant formation or continuance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No per-day late fee is prescribed; failure to file for two consecutive years may lead the Director to dissolve the corporation administratively after notice. A CBCA offence summary conviction may carry a fine of up to CAD 5,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises — required for every enterprise registered in the Quebec enterprise register, including QBCA provincial corporations and extra-provincial corporations carrying on activity in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the enterprise's registration in the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; online filing is available throughout the 60-day window.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years may result in cancellation of registration by REQ after notice; cancellation of a legal person's registration causes loss of legal capacity to carry on activities and requires reinstatement. Administrative late-filing charges may also apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Franchise annual registration or annual franchise filing for Quebec master franchise operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None applicable — Quebec does not operate a franchise registration or annual franchise filing system; franchise obligations derive from contract and the Civil Code of Quebec.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No statutory annual deadline in Quebec. A franchise disclosure document must be delivered before signing franchise agreements in Canadian disclosure provinces outside Quebec if franchises are offered there.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No Quebec filing penalty applies; in disclosure provinces, failure to deliver a compliant franchise disclosure document can create statutory rescission rights and damage claims for franchisees.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Neither the CBCA nor the QBCA imposes an automatic audit based on revenue, assets, or employee count. A distributing or public corporation must appoint an independent auditor annually. A non-distributing private corporation may dispense with an audit only through the waiver mechanism permitted by the governing act, typically unanimous shareholder consent; absent a valid waiver, an auditor must be appointed at each annual meeting. The master franchise agreement may independently require an annual audit or review of central kitchen and royalty statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with Canadian generally accepted accounting principles. Publicly accountable enterprises must apply IFRS as set out in Part I of the CPA Canada Handbook; private enterprises may apply IFRS or the Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) in Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook. A bakery master franchise group normally applies ASPE.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not require a separate public annual UBO declaration. When shareholdings transfer, the corporate secretary must obtain seller and buyer confirmation, secure director approval where required, record the transfer in the share transfer register and register of members, and amend the Quebec enterprise register if the registered legal-participation or director data changes. For CBCA corporations, an individual with significant control (ISC) register must be maintained and updated within 15 days of any change in significant control; the annual return is not a substitute for the ISC register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (where CBCA applies)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–700 per year for Quebec registered office, registered agent, and basic corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000–18,000 for a small to mid-sized bakery franchise group with central kitchen; USD 3,500–8,000 for a review engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined general corporate rate: 26.5% (federal 15% net of provincial abatement + Quebec 11.5%). Active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) up to CAD 500,000: combined 12.2% (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2%), subject to phase-out based on taxable capital and passive income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction reduces the federal rate to 9% on the first CAD 500,000; Quebec equivalent reduces its rate to 3.2% on the same business income; Manufacturing and Processing Profits deduction reduces the federal general rate to 13% for qualifying central-kitchen food production; federal SR&ED refundable investment tax credits (15% to 35% for qualifying R&D) and Quebec refundable innovation credits (30% for certain R&D in food processing); Quebec refundable tax credits for manufacturing and e-commerce/digital transformation may also apply to POS and online bakery systems.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return transmitted electronically via CRA-approved tax preparation software through E-file or CRA My Business Account. Provincial: CO-17 Corporation Tax Return transmitted to Revenu Québec through its authorized e-filing service for corporations (Entreprise in Revenu Québec online services).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (T2 and CO-17 once per taxation year). Corporate income tax instalments are generally payable monthly; GST/QST returns are remitted monthly or quarterly depending on sales revenue; payroll source deductions for bakery staff are remitted on a regular statutory schedule.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 and CO-17 must be filed by the last day of the 6th month following the fiscal year-end (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 year-end). The balance of corporate income tax is due by the last day of the 2nd month after fiscal year-end, or the 3rd month for an eligible CCPC whose taxable income is at or below the small business limit. Monthly instalments are due throughout the year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue: aggregate of point-of-sale bakery sales, master franchise income (initial fees and ongoing royalties), central kitchen intercompany sales to franchisees, online catering, and other business income, reported in Canadian dollars.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record intercompany revenues from or to non-resident franchisees at arm's length prices consistent with the transfer pricing policy; do not net costs; report on a gross basis and reconcile with GST/QST revenue declared to Revenu Québec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses: cost of goods sold (flour, ingredients, packaging), employee wages and benefits, owner and director salaries, rent, marketing and franchise services, depreciation (CCA), insurance, repairs, franchise royalties paid to the master franchisor, and interest on debt financing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border royalties, management fees, and interest paid or credited to a non-resident related party must be reported in the Part XIII reconciliation and disclosed in T2 Schedule 1; expenses lacking economic substance or contemporaneous benchmarking may be denied under section 247(2), section 18(1)(b), or the Quebec equivalent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: determined after all Schedule 1 (federal) and Schedule G (Quebec) additions and deductions, including non-capital loss carryovers, capital gains and losses, dividend adjustments, and any dividend refund or refundable dividend tax on hand (RDTOH/ERDTOH) reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Canadian-resident corporation reports worldwide income; foreign tax credits are claimed using the applicable T2 schedules. If a residency dispute arises under the Canada-China treaty, corroborate central management and control with board minutes, strategic decision records, and physical presence in Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital Cost Allowance (CCA) computations, recaptures and terminal losses, non-capital loss utilization, allowable business investment losses, and Quebec-specific adjustments such as investment tax credits or provincial innovation deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the correct CCA classes for bakery ovens, refrigeration, POS systems, and leasehold improvements; ensure government subsidies or non-repayable contributions reduce the capital cost base; retain Quebec-specific credit forms and source documentation for audit trail.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid federal tax balance plus 1% per full month of delay (maximum 12%); repeat offence: 10% plus 2% per month (maximum 24%). Quebec applies an equivalent 5% plus 1% per month penalty under the Tax Administration Act. Late or deficient instalments attract compound daily interest at the CRA/Revenu Québec prescribed rate. Failure to file an information return (e.g., T5 summary, Part XIII non-resident payment reconciliation, or foreign reporting forms) triggers CAD 100 per day up to CAD 2,500 per return, in addition to the general late-filing penalty.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the federal Income Tax Act, applicable to dividends paid or credited by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder; a corresponding Quebec tax is levied on the same base.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Under the Canada-China Income Tax Agreement (1986, as amended by the 2011 Protocol), Article 10 reduces the dividend withholding rate to 15% for portfolio shareholders and to 10% where the beneficial owner is a company (other than a partnership) that beneficially owns at least 10% of the voting shares of the Canadian payer. Process: the non-resident shareholder must provide the Quebec paying corporation with CRA Form NR301 (Statement of Eligibility for Treaty Benefits) together with a valid Chinese Certificate of Residence for Tax issued by the State Taxation Administration confirming residence for the relevant calendar year. The Canadian payer may withhold at the treaty rate only if the completed documentation is received before payment; otherwise, 25% must be withheld and the non-resident may file a refund claim with CRA using Form NR7-R.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate is 25% for both interest and royalties. Under the Canada-China treaty, interest is limited to 10% and royalties are limited to 10%. Royalties include payments of any kind for the use of or right to use trademarks, franchise rights, recipes, technical know-how, and industrial design. The interest limitation applies to debt claims and is subject to thin capitalization rules (section 18(4)) and the general limitation-of-benefits analysis.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File / contemporaneous TP documentation is required where the total annual gross revenue from transactions with a single non-arm's length non-resident reaches or exceeds CAD 1,000,000. Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required for multinational enterprise groups with consolidated revenue of CAD 1,100,000,000 or more, consistent with CRA's OECD-aligned filing requirements.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada and Quebec do not enact a separate Economic Substance Regulations statute of the kind found in zero-corporate-tax jurisdictions. However, the federal General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s. 245 ITA), the Quebec GAAR equivalent, the common law sham doctrine, and the central management and control test for corporate residence jointly require demonstrable economic substance. A Chinese pastry bakery chain that centralizes trademark ownership, intercompany royalty streams, and a central kitchen in Quebec must show physical premises, local employees, active board decision-making in Canada, and real operational risk. A structure that is a bare conduit or letterbox company will be re-characterized, the royalty deduction denied, and the 50% GAAR penalty imposed in addition to reassessed tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fraudulently omitting cash sales from bakery POS terminals, operating shadow cash registers, deleting end-of-day Z-reports, paying staff off the books, or deliberately understating master franchise royalty revenue on the T2/CO-17 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal: Income Tax Act s. 239(1) – fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to 5 years; gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax under s. 163(2). Quebec: Tax Administration Act – penalty of 50% of the evaded tax and imprisonment for up to 5 years. The CRA Voluntary Disclosures Program will deny relief where the non-disclosure was wilful.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who directed or participated in the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax, fines, and restitution; they face personal criminal prosecution, imprisonment, CRA jeopardy orders freezing assets, and court-ordered travel bans preventing departure from Canada while the assessment is in dispute.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Quebec corporation that functions merely as a letterbox for the Chinese master franchisor: no real employees, no physical bakery premises, board meetings held offshore, and all substantive commercial decisions made in China while the Canadian entity books royalty deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s. 245 ITA) empowers CRA to deny the tax benefit and re-characterize the whole arrangement; a 50% penalty applies to the tax benefit obtained. Revenu Québec applies a parallel provincial GAAR. At common law the arrangement may be void as a sham, and CRA may disregard the corporate entity and assess the foreign principal directly on Canadian-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil exposes directors to personal liability for corporate debts, unremitted source deductions, and GST/QST. Directors who knowingly sign false or misleading returns face criminal fines and imprisonment under s. 239; the courts may also impose personal restitution equal to the tax avoided.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging a master franchise royalty exceeding 5% of gross sales and a central kitchen markup above arm's length to related Quebec franchisees without a benchmark study or contemporaneous TP documentation, or failing to prepare a Local File despite cross-border intercompany flows exceeding CAD 1,000,000 in one taxation year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reassess the royalty and markup to an arm's length amount under s. 247(2); a 10% penalty under s. 247(3) applies to the net transfer pricing adjustment where the adjustment exceeds the lesser of CAD 5,000,000 or 10% of the taxpayer's gross revenue. Compound daily interest accrues from the date the return was due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve inflated intercompany royalties or who sign declarations containing false TP information may be assessed for gross negligence; the corporate penalty attaches first, but directors may be pursued where the overpayment is combined with unpaid source deductions or GST/QST, and criminal prosecution is available in cases of deliberate falsification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash payments from franchisees or bakery distributors structured to avoid the CAD 10,000 large-cash-transaction reporting threshold, or failing to submit a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) when franchise store deposits show layering patterns, rapid cross-border wires, or repeated split-cash deposits from the same beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, FINTRAC may impose an administrative monetary penalty of up to CAD 500,000 per violation on a corporation; criminal conviction is punishable by a fine of up to CAD 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years. Revenu Québec may additionally assess penalties for undeclared cash income and unreported GST/QST.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who directed or authorized the concealment may be prosecuted individually, with personal fines and imprisonment upon conviction. They are also personally liable for the corporation's unremitted GST/QST and payroll source deductions where the cash scheme is part of a deliberate plan to suppress taxable sales.
